why: Inserting the fallback that prefers cuts immediately after essential post‑nominal modifiers (C_end) made the model avoid cutting between a head and its following modifier, which improved cohesion for very short pieces (bins ≤3 and ≤5) but caused many cuts to shift into nearby positions (earlier or later) that split other noun+modifier pairs or enumerations, producing several large negative tail moves and a near‑zero net gain.
lesson: Keep the fallback's benefit for very short pieces (≤5) while ensuring it does not simply relocate cuts to adjacent noun/modifier or list boundaries where it creates new splits.
